title: Things to Do in Bhubaneswar: Kalinga Temples, Jain Caves & Odisha's Crafts
seoTitle: Things to Do in Bhubaneswar: Temples, Caves & More | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Bhubaneswar: the Lingaraj, Mukteshwar, Rajarani and Parashurameswar temples, Bindu Sagar, Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves, Dhauli's Ashokan edicts, the Chausath Yogini temple at Hirapur, Nandankanan, the State and Tribal museums, Ekamra Haat and Odia food.
dek: The capital of Odisha and an ancient temple city, where hundreds of Kalinga-style temples, 2,000-year-old Jain caves and an Ashokan rock edict sit within a modern planned city.
searchIntent: Travellers spending one or two days in Bhubaneswar, often as part of a Puri–Konark circuit.

hero.caption: Mukteshwar Temple

intro: Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, is often called the Temple City of India. Hundreds of stone temples were built here between about the 7th and 13th centuries in the Kalinga style, with curved towers (deul) covered in carvings. The city's history goes back further still: the Jain caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri date from the 2nd century BCE, and at nearby Dhauli, Emperor Ashoka's edicts mark the aftermath of the Kalinga war.

The things to do in Bhubaneswar include the great Lingaraj Temple and the jewel-like Mukteshwar and Rajarani temples, the rock-cut Jain caves, the peace pagoda at Dhauli, the circular yogini temple at Hirapur, museums, crafts and Odia food. Puri and Konark are close by.
One to two days is enough for the city. October to March is the best time.

items.name: See the Lingaraj Temple

image.alt: Tower of the Lingaraj Temple, Bhubaneswar
image.caption: Lingaraj Temple

body: The Lingaraj Temple, built in the 11th century, is the largest temple in Bhubaneswar, with a tower about 55 metres high in a walled compound of over 100 smaller shrines. It is dedicated to Harihara, a combined form of Shiva and Vishnu. Entry is restricted to Hindus; non-Hindus can view the temple from a platform outside the wall.

items.name: Visit the Mukteshwar Temple
body: The Mukteshwar Temple, from the 10th century, is small but exquisitely carved, with a famous arched gateway (torana) and sculptures of ascetics, animals and folk tales. It is often called the gem of Odisha architecture. The Mukteshwar Dance Festival is held here in January.

items.name: See the Rajarani Temple

image.alt: Rajarani Temple in a garden, Bhubaneswar
image.caption: Rajarani Temple

body: The Rajarani Temple, from around the 11th century, is named after the red-gold sandstone used to build it. It has no deity inside, and its tower is covered with graceful carvings of women and guardians of the eight directions. The Rajarani Music Festival is held here in January.

items.name: Visit Parashurameswar and Brahmeswar
body: The Parashurameswar Temple, from the 7th century, is one of the oldest surviving temples in the city. Brahmeswar Temple, from the 11th century, is a well-preserved example of a five-shrine (panchayatana) plan.

items.name: Walk around Bindu Sagar
body: Bindu Sagar, a large temple tank near Lingaraj, is believed to hold water from sacred rivers. The Ananta Vasudeva Temple on its bank is known for its kitchen, like Puri's.

items.name: Explore Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves
body: The twin hills of Udayagiri and Khandagiri have rock-cut chambers carved for Jain monks, mostly in the 2nd century BCE under King Kharavela. The two-storey Rani Gumpha has fine friezes, and the Hathigumpha inscription records Kharavela's reign. Khandagiri has a Jain temple on top.

items.name: See Dhauli
body: At Dhauli, about 8 km south, a rock carries edicts of Emperor Ashoka, carved after the bloody Kalinga war of around 261 BCE, which led him to embrace Buddhism. A white Shanti Stupa (peace pagoda), built with Japanese help, crowns the hill, and a light and sound show is held in the evening.

items.name: Visit the Chausath Yogini Temple
body: At Hirapur, about 15 km away, a small circular open-air temple from the 9th century holds 64 carved figures of yoginis, female deities, in niches around the wall. It is one of only a few such temples in India.

items.name: See white tigers at Nandankanan
body: Nandankanan Zoological Park, on the city's edge, is known for its white tigers and runs lion and tiger safaris. It also has a botanical garden and a lake. It is closed on Mondays.

items.name: Visit the State and Tribal museums
body: The Odisha State Museum has palm-leaf manuscripts, sculptures and coins. The Museum of Tribal Arts and Artefacts has displays on Odisha's 62 tribal communities, with textiles, ornaments and tools.

items.name: Shop at Ekamra Haat
body: Ekamra Haat is a crafts market selling Odisha's handlooms, including Sambalpuri ikat and Bomkai saris, silver filigree from Cuttack, pattachitra and stone carvings.

items.name: Eat Odia food
body: Try dalma (lentils cooked with vegetables), pakhala (fermented rice, especially in summer), machha besara (fish in mustard), and chhena poda, a baked cottage cheese sweet. Odisha's rasagola has its own GI tag.

items.name: October to March
body: Pleasant weather and the festival season, with dance and music festivals at the temples in January.

items.name: April to June
body: Very hot and humid; sightsee in the early morning.

items.name: July to September
body: Monsoon rain, and the Rath Yatra in nearby Puri in June or July.

byTraveller.text: The temples, Udayagiri and Khandagiri, Dhauli and Hirapur.
Nandankanan, the State Museum and Dhauli's evening show.
Ekamra Haat, the Tribal Museum and a temple dance festival in January.

oneDay: Start at Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves in the morning, then visit the Lingaraj, Mukteshwar and Rajarani temples. After an Odia lunch, see the Tribal Museum, and end at Dhauli for sunset and the light show.
tips: Biju Patnaik International Airport and Bhubaneswar railway station are close to the city centre.
Temples are best visited in the early morning, before the heat.
Dress modestly and remove shoes at temples.
Combine with Puri and Konark for a three- or four-day circuit.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Bhubaneswar?
faqs.a: See the Lingaraj, Mukteshwar and Rajarani temples, explore Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves, visit Dhauli and the Chausath Yogini Temple, see Nandankanan and the museums, and eat Odia food.

faqs.q: Can non-Hindus enter the Lingaraj Temple?
faqs.a: No, but they can view it from a platform outside the compound wall.
